text.p: COPENHAGEN, Sept 23 (Reuter) Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Minister of finance Mogens Lykketoft has rejected a new business report showing that the chronically unemployed have not been taken care of. Lykketoft does not think the report which is to be published in two weeks as part of an annual study of Danish business is good enough.
--- Danish researchers have found a new scanning technique which will make it possible to diagnose depression with more certainty and determine the best treament. POLITIKEN

--- The fear that Danish firms are moving still more of their production to low-wage areas in Eastern Europe and Asia seems to be exaggerated as new central bank figures show that investments in these areas are starting to decrease after a small increase within the last couple of years. Last year direct Danish investments in Eastern Europe, Asia, Latin America and Africa ended at 2.8 billion while investments in the same countries within the first six months of 1996 only ended at 1.0 billion.

--- With new rules from labour market authorities people who are unemployed now risk losing their unemployment benefits if they show up drunk or very untidy at job centres which according to job market authorities makes them unavailable for work.
--- Liberal chairman Uffe Elleman-Jensen advises against a quick referendum on the four Danish EU optouts. There is too much Danish scepticism and the chances of a vote to overturn the optouts.

--- A large group of second generation immigrant children start school with no Danish skills. Local authorities are shocked at the lacking skills which have not improved in spite of more immigrant children spending time with Danish children before entering school.
--- Home electronic securities trading is about to be introduced in Denmark as one out of three Danes now say that they are ready to trade and pay via the Internet.
